channel.title: Hanceville Entertainment and Shopping - Local News
channel.description: Hanceville, AL news from city hall, local schools, sports, public safety and weather in Cullman County. Every story is dated and links to its sources.

item.title: Freeze warnings tonight and Saturday night: lows near 26 in Cullman County
item.description: The National Weather Service in Huntsville has issued two Freeze Warnings, from midnight to 8 AM Saturday and again from midnight to 8 AM Sunday, with temperatures as low as 26 degrees.

item.title: Good Hope, Vinemont and Cold Springs play for quarterfinal spots tonight
item.description: Good Hope hosts No. 9 Deshler, Vinemont hosts Fayette County and No. 10 Cold Springs visits Lexington in the second round of the AHSAA football playoffs. All three games kick off at 7 PM.

item.title: Colony fixes its library windows and sets a Christmas tree lighting, a pajama game night and a cemetery cleanup
item.description: The Colony Town Council approved window repairs at the town library on Nov. 10 and announced holiday plans, including a tree lighting Dec. 6 and a pajama Christmas game night Dec. 19. A library board meeting and a cemetery cleanup with a fish fry are set for Saturday, Nov. 14.

item.title: School report cards are out: Hanceville High climbs to 89 and Cullman County keeps its A
item.description: Alabama's 2025-26 school report cards, released Nov. 12, give Cullman County Schools a 91 and another A. Hanceville High rose four points to 89, and Cullman City Schools set a record with a 97.

item.title: Cullman High Theatre wins Best in Show, and you can see the show this weekend
item.description: Cullman High School Theatre won Best in Show at the District 3 Walter Trumbauer festival with "James and the Giant Peach." Public shows are Friday and Saturday, Nov. 13 and 14, at 7 PM.

item.title: Kenneth Walker and Richard Barnett join the Cullman County Commission
item.description: The two new commissioners were sworn in Wednesday, Nov. 11, succeeding Kerry Watson and Garry Marchman, who each served 12 years. Their first work session is Tuesday, Nov. 17, at 4 PM.

item.title: Cullman County Public Library adds a campaign manager for its $1 million Every Chapter Matters drive and wants your input
item.description: The library's Every Chapter Matters campaign aims to raise $1 million to renovate and expand its 1967 building. New campaign manager Laney Hulsey says a community survey is open now, and help can mean volunteering or spreading the word, not just donating.

item.title: Cullman council takes first look tonight at tougher rules and $2,500 fines to protect its drinking water lakes
item.description: The Cullman City Council gives Ordinance 2026-56 a first reading at 6 PM Monday, Nov. 9. It would update protections for Lake Catoma, Lake George and Duck River Reservoir and raise the minimum fine to $2,500 per violation.

item.title: City of Cullman brings back compost pickup starting Saturday, Nov. 14
item.description: Cullman residents can pick up fresh compost at the city's sanitation sites again starting Nov. 14, made from leaves collected by the city's vacuum leaf trucks. Fees start at $25 for a car or pickup.

item.title: Cullman's Christmas Open House weekend starts Friday with Santa, a free Cookie Crawl and a pickle hunt
item.description: The Cullman Area Chamber of Commerce kicks off holiday shopping Nov. 13 to 15. Santa visits the Chamber from 4 to 6 PM Friday, the free Cookie Crawl runs Saturday from 10 AM to 2 PM, and shops hide Christmas pickles on Sunday.

item.title: Cullman sets Nov. 17 as Retired Teachers Day, so thank a teacher
item.description: Mayor Woody Jacobs signed a proclamation naming Tuesday, Nov. 17, Retired Teachers Day in the City of Cullman. Members of the Cullman Education Retirees Association accepted it on Nov. 5.

item.title: Cullman planners hold off on a 7 Brew drive thru near schools until December
item.description: The Cullman Planning Commission tabled a plan to add a 7 Brew Coffee at 800 Second Ave. NW after commissioners raised traffic concerns near schools. The item comes back Dec. 1, and two annexations along U.S. 278 and Highway 157 got favorable votes.

item.title: Work starts on Bella Balle, a new condo and shop building in downtown Cullman
item.description: Construction has begun on Bella Balle Condominiums, a three story building on Fourth Street SE with ground floor commercial space and four condos above. The project is expected to take 12 to 14 months.

item.title: Shrimp Basket closes its Cullman restaurant as the chain refocuses on the coast
item.description: Artistry Restaurants shuttered the Cullman Shrimp Basket effective Nov. 1, part of a wider pullback from inland locations so the brand can put its energy into beach and coastal stores.

item.title: Cullman Regional Lights of Love returns Dec. 8 to honor hospice patients and Dr. Marecle
item.description: The Cullman Regional Foundation will hold its Dr. Herman C. Ensor Lights of Love Ceremony on Tuesday, Dec. 8 at 6 p.m. at St. John's Evangelical Protestant Church, with gifts lighting the hospital Christmas tree.

item.title: Wallace State welcomes area first graders for Let's Pretend Hospital
item.description: Nursing students and the Hanceville Fire Department turned the School of Nursing into kid friendly stations this week so first graders could learn about hospitals, fire safety and healthy habits without the scare.

item.title: Jack's Western founder Larry Allred named Bronze Alabama Retailer of the Year
item.description: The Alabama Retail Association honored Good Hope's Larry Allred for five decades building Jack's Western and Outdoor Wear into a nearly 30,000-square-foot destination that still feels like a family store.

item.title: Hanceville High gets $7,000 for woodwind instruments in county grant round
item.description: AMRV RC&D and the Cullman County Legislative Delegation awarded $104,859 across 13 local projects. Hanceville High School's share buys and restores woodwind instruments for the band.

item.title: Veterans Day weekend in Cullman County: airport celebration, fireworks and a Wallace State salute
item.description: Free festivities run from Saturday through Tuesday, with the Cullman Regional Airport celebration Nov. 7, fireworks at Good Hope Park on Sunday, and Wallace State's Salute to United States Veterans concert Nov. 10.

item.title: Holly Pond clears Lions Club land deal to renovate park fields, eyes playground at Governor's Park
item.description: Mayor Carla Hart told the town council on Nov. 2 that Holly Pond finalized buying about one acre from the Lions Club, unlocking a $91,000 fencing package for Lions Club Park. Council also backed looking at small playground gear for Governor's Park after the new year.

item.title: Wallace State men's soccer wins Southeast District title, punches ticket to nationals in Huntsville
item.description: The Lions beat Patrick and Henry 6-5 on penalty kicks after 110 scoreless minutes on Oct. 31. Goalkeeper Emrik Senecal's final save sent Wallace State to the NJCAA Division II national tournament, which starts Nov. 15 in Huntsville.

item.title: Wallace State men and women sweep ACCC cross country for a ninth straight year
item.description: Both Lion teams won ACCC titles on Oct. 30 at John Hunt Park in Huntsville. Brookelyn Morgan took the women's individual crown, and Jaquavion Bryant led the men with a runner-up finish.

item.title: Hanceville's That Thrift Store has last minute Halloween costumes from 59 cents and a $5 fill a bag deal all year
item.description: The family owned shop at 914 Main Street NE prices costumes from 59 cents to $5 and lets shoppers fill a bag with clothes for $5, with holiday decor priced low ahead of Thanksgiving and Christmas.

item.title: Last call: Parkside Outreach Program's Christmas Coalition takes applications through Sunday, Nov. 1
item.description: The Baileyton nonprofit helps local families in need with Christmas for their children. Applications are due Nov. 1, and sponsors can adopt an angel for $25.

item.title: Voting Tuesday? Hanceville's polls are at City Hall and the Civic Center, open 7 AM to 7 PM
item.description: The Nov. 3 general election notice lists Hanceville City Hall for Precinct 3, Box 1 and Hanceville Civic Center for Precinct 3, Box 2. Bring a photo ID and check your assigned spot before you go.

item.title: What's on the Nov. 3 ballot in Hanceville: state races, a school board seat and a county tax freeze for homeowners 65 and up
item.description: Hanceville voters will see federal and state races, the Hanceville seat on the Cullman County Board of Education, county offices, four statewide amendments and one Cullman County amendment that would freeze home values for qualifying seniors.

item.title: Cullman County remembers Eddie Wilson, who built The Foundry Farm into a place for men to rebuild their lives
item.description: The longtime director of The Foundry Ministries' farm between Holly Pond and Berlin died Oct. 28. Visitation is today from noon to 2 PM at The Foundry Farm Chapel, with a celebration of life at 2 PM.

item.title: Cullman Regional gets $2.5 million in federal money for a surgical robot
item.description: The hospital will use a federal grant secured by Sen. Katie Britt to buy a da Vinci surgical robot, bringing more minimally invasive surgery options close to home.

item.title: Good Hope and Vinemont head to the playoffs as Cullman County football wraps up the regular season
item.description: Friday night closed the regular season for most county teams. Good Hope travels to Fairfield and Vinemont visits Central Florence in the first round on Nov. 6.

item.title: Wren + Revel is closing its Cullman children's boutique, with Saturday, Oct. 31, as the last day
item.description: The Warehouse District shop at 103 First Ave. NE says all remaining sales are final.

item.title: West Point volleyball reaches the state semifinals as Addison wins its 16th state title
item.description: West Point and Cold Springs closed their seasons at the state tournament in Birmingham, and neighboring Addison beat Meek for a second straight Class 1A championship.

item.title: About 1,600 eighth graders try out careers at Wallace State's Tools of the Trade
item.description: Students from Cullman, Blount and Winston counties spent Tuesday on the Hanceville campus trying hands on stations in health care, manufacturing, skilled trades and more.

item.title: Wallace State's first Entrepreneurship Event gives students a front row seat to starting a business
item.description: Karma's Coffee House and Jubilee Kitchen and Bar owner Katie Fine, a Wallace State graduate, told students in Hanceville that courage and the right people around you matter more than knowing everything.

item.title: Library's Spooktacular 5K draws more than 300 runners, raises over $15,000 and kicks off an expansion campaign
item.description: The Cullman County Public Library is launching Every Chapter Matters, a campaign for a renovated and expanded library.

item.title: Cullman County Public Library opens a November short story challenge for writers of every age
item.description: Writers of all ages can enter a story of 1,000 to 5,000 words from Nov. 2 through Nov. 25, and the library hosts a free writing workshop on Nov. 4.

item.title: Signed minutes from the Oct. 8 council meeting show new park addresses, a $30 Holly Market vendor fee and a pool leak
item.description: The city posted the official minutes from the Oct. 8 Hanceville City Council meeting. They list new addresses planned for C.W. Day Park and the pool, a $30 fee for Holly Market vendors, and a pool leak crews still have not found.

item.title: Hanceville council tables vehicle policy, passes credit card rules and moves its Thanksgiving meeting to Nov. 24
item.description: At its Oct. 22 meeting the council put the take home vehicle policy on hold for six months, approved a city credit card policy and a $50,500 Public Works tractor, and set holiday dates for Veterans Park.

item.title: Dry skies for Friday night trunk or treats, but showers are likely on Halloween night
item.description: The National Weather Service calls for a mostly cloudy, mild Friday night, then a 30 percent chance of showers Saturday afternoon that climbs to 60 percent after dark on Halloween.

item.title: Good Hope's planned hotel waits on a gas line under I-65 as a new package store gets ready to open
item.description: Mayor Jerry Bartlett says a hotel planned off County Road 490 is on hold until natural gas can cross the interstate, while a new package store across from the Scotty Hooper Museum nears its opening.

item.title: A $50,000 Lowe's grant will turn the Cullman County Public Library's back lawn into a play area and outdoor reading space
item.description: The main library on Clark Street is one of 100 nonprofits nationwide picked for a 2026 Lowe's Community Impact Grant, and it hopes to break ground within a couple of weeks.

item.title: Cullman names November Hospice and Palliative Care Month and thanks the people who care for families
item.description: Mayor Woody Jacobs signed the proclamation with Hospice of North Alabama, one of several hospice providers serving the Cullman area.

item.title: Cullman council approves County Road 616 annexation, an AI services contract and two E-911 grant applications
item.description: The Cullman City Council also bought electronic signature service, moved employee dental coverage and set its next meeting for Nov. 9.

item.title: Cold Springs sweeps cross country sectionals as five county teams head to state, and Hanceville's runners finish the season
item.description: Cold Springs, both Cullman squads and the Holly Pond girls earned team berths for the Nov. 7 state meet in Moulton, while the Hanceville boys placed ninth in Class 3A Section 3.

item.title: Cold Springs routs Tanner 57 to 20 for its first nine win season since 1993 and hosts Pisgah in the playoffs
item.description: Cooper Johnson ran for three touchdowns on senior night as the No. 10 Eagles closed the regular season at 9 and 1.

item.title: Elkmont beats Hanceville 48 to 8 as the Bulldogs close out the 2026 season
item.description: Hanceville scored in the fourth quarter Friday night at Elkmont but could not catch up, finishing the season 0 and 10.

item.title: Two Cullman shops grow: Arboreadum Bookshop and Garden celebrates its grand opening and Gamer Geeks doubles its space
item.description: A bookstore in a remodeled downtown house and a game store on St. Joseph Drive both have more room for neighbors to gather.

item.title: About 500 seniors filled the fairgrounds for Senior Day at the Cullman County Fair
item.description: The Cullman County Commission on Aging says roughly 500 people 55 and older came out Wednesday for free admission, a free lunch, live music and a moment honoring veterans.

item.title: Mud Creek Arts and Crafts Festival returns to downtown Hanceville Nov. 7
item.description: The free street festival marks its 16th year on Commercial Street from 9 AM to 4 PM, and vendor booths and sponsorships are still open.

item.title: Friday night roundup: Addison wins region title, Vinemont clinches seventh straight playoff trip
item.description: Addison finished a perfect 10 and 0 regular season with a Class 1A, Region 7 title, Vinemont rallied late to make the playoffs again, and Cold Springs, Cullman and Good Hope all won big on the last region night of the season.

item.title: Cold Springs and West Point volleyball head to the state tournament next week
item.description: Both Cullman County teams won five set third place matches at the North Super Regional in Hoover and will play in the state quarterfinals at the Birmingham CrossPlex on Wednesday, Oct. 28. For Cold Springs, it is the first state trip since 1989.

item.title: Wallace State volleyball wins 14 straight and heads to the conference tournament at 30 and 5
item.description: The Lions swept all five matches in the past week, including a home doubleheader with Southern Union on Thursday, and open ACCC tournament play in Montgomery on Oct. 31.

item.title: Wallace State sets a new fall enrollment record with 7,141 students
item.description: Hanceville's community college topped 7,100 students for the first time in its history, its fourth straight fall increase. Spring 2027 registration is open now.

item.title: Shakespeare, The Nutcracker and a veterans concert lead Wallace State's new arts season
item.description: Wallace State's Fine and Performing Arts program posted its 2026 and 2027 lineup. Several shows are free, and the season opens Nov. 6 with Much Ado About Nothing.

item.title: Sunny weekend ahead: trunk or treats, a barbecue cookoff and the last day of the county fair
item.description: Forecasters expect sunshine and highs in the low 70s through Sunday, which lines up nicely with a packed weekend of family fun across Cullman County.

item.title: Sheriff's environmental deputy pulls up to 35 tons of trash a year off Cullman County roads
item.description: Deputy Ron Wood and the sheriff's litter crew clean about 100 miles of county roads each year, and money from the recyclables they collect goes to local nonprofits.

item.title: County Commission pays for tornado siren repairs, adopts a five year hazard plan and thanks two departing members
item.description: At its Oct. 20 meeting the Cullman County Commission approved about $39,000 in siren repairs, a new Hazard Mitigation Plan, a lower speed limit on County Road 52 and new cabins at Stony Lonesome OHV Park.

item.title: Country Wok adds ramen, Hong Kong wontons and a matcha cannoli to its downtown Hanceville menu
item.description: Owner Kenny Lee keeps the menu small and the ingredients local, and he just added four new dishes at 107 Bangor Ave. Open Tuesday through Saturday, 11 a.m. to 7 p.m.

item.title: Christmas plans, a storm prep tax holiday and hiring rules filled Hanceville's Oct. 22 council agenda
item.description: The city posted the agenda for Thursday's council meeting. It lists the downtown trunk or treat, the Christmas parade and tree lighting, a severe weather sales tax holiday resolution and a plan to move the Thanksgiving Day meeting.

item.title: Bulldogs host 8 and 1 Oneonta tonight at Ray Talley Stadium
item.description: Hanceville plays its final home game of the season Friday at 7 p.m. against one of the top teams in Class 3A, Region 6. Skies should be clear and cool.

item.title: Oneonta beats Hanceville 62 to 0; Bulldogs close the season at Elkmont next Friday
item.description: The Bulldogs fell to 8 and 1 Oneonta in their final home game of the year Friday night at Ray Talley Stadium. Hanceville wraps up the regular season Oct. 30 at Elkmont.

item.title: Hanceville weekend weather: sunny days, cold nights
item.description: The National Weather Service expects sunshine Saturday through Monday in Hanceville, with highs in the 60s and lows near 40. Saturday will be windy.

item.title: Wallace State volleyball has won nine straight heading into Saturday
item.description: The Lions swept Bishop State and Lurleen B. Wallace on Friday and finish their home invitational Saturday with matches at 11 a.m. and 3 p.m. at Tom Drake Coliseum.

item.title: Register to vote by Monday, Oct. 19, and get to know the five amendments on the Nov. 3 ballot
item.description: Monday is the last day to register for the Nov. 3 general election. Cullman County voters will also decide four statewide amendments and one local question about freezing property values for qualifying seniors.

item.title: Cullman marks MS Awareness Day with a free walk at Heritage Park today
item.description: Mayor Woody Jacobs proclaimed Oct. 17 Multiple Sclerosis Awareness Day. The Move Over MS Walk runs 8 a.m. to noon at Heritage Park with music, free snacks and a kids costume contest.

item.title: Listerhill Credit Union opens its new Cullman branch and gives $10,000 to Cullman County Schools
item.description: The credit union held a grand opening Thursday at 702 Industrial Dr. SW and handed Superintendent Dr. Shane Barnette a $10,000 check for the county school system.

item.title: Hanceville High's National Honor Society chapter wins national recognition
item.description: The Hanceville High chapter earned the National Honor Society's Chapter of Distinction award for leadership and service to the school and town.

item.title: Hanceville High on fall break through Monday, Red Ribbon Week starts Oct. 26
item.description: Hanceville High students are out Friday, Oct. 16, and Monday, Oct. 19. Red Ribbon Week runs Oct. 26 to 30 with a different dress up theme each day.

item.title: Young performers can audition Oct. 20 for the For Kids' Sake Variety Show
item.description: The Cullman Regional Foundation is looking for singers, dancers, musicians and other young talent for its 2027 show, which raises money for nursery and pediatric care at Cullman Regional.

item.title: Curt's Closet is collecting toys for up to 600 Cullman County kids this Christmas
item.description: The local nonprofit's annual Curt's Christmas toy drive runs through mid November. You can drop off new toys at three spots in Cullman and Vinemont or sign up as a sponsor.

item.title: Meet your Hanceville City Council before the Nov. 12 meeting
item.description: Hanceville's five council members and the Mayor meet next on Thursday, Nov. 12, at City Hall. Here is who represents you and how to follow along.

item.title: Hanceville council adds $25,000 for road patching, backs mayor on fire chief
item.description: More gas tax money is going toward potholes, a take home vehicle policy is still up for debate, and the council upheld the mayor's removal of the fire chief. The next meeting is Thursday, Oct. 22, at 6 p.m.

item.title: Hanceville's Cipollari siblings will play a free Randy Travis Foundation benefit Nov. 7
item.description: The six sibling bluegrass band from Hanceville performs Saturday, Nov. 7, from 6 to 8 p.m. at Terri Pines Country Club in Cullman. Tickets are free.

item.title: Bulldogs fall to Hokes Bluff, host Oneonta next Friday at Ray Talley Stadium
item.description: Hokes Bluff beat Hanceville 49 to 8 in a Class 3A, Region 6 game that was moved up to Thursday because of fall break. Oneonta comes to town Friday, Oct. 23, at 7 p.m.

item.title: America's Thrift Stores plans a November opening in Cullman and is hiring now
item.description: The secondhand store is moving into the former Bargain Hunt space at 1721 Second Ave. SW, and donations there support Make A Wish Alabama.

item.title: Youth Leadership students harvest and cook their own lunch at the Agriplex
item.description: Students in the Cullman Area Chamber's Youth Leadership program picked vegetables and cooked a meal in the North Alabama Agriplex teaching kitchen.

item.title: City posts official records from the Oct. 8 council meeting
item.description: The City of Hanceville shares records from each council meeting on its website. The latest set covers the Oct. 8 meeting.

item.title: State fire marshal investigating fire at St. John Missionary Baptist Church
item.description: An early morning fire on Monday, Oct. 5, left the Hanceville church badly damaged. The Alabama State Fire Marshal's Office is looking into the cause, which has not been released.

item.title: Hanceville's new budget expects about $5.46 million in revenue
item.description: The city budget for October 2026 through September 2027 plans for roughly $5.46 million coming in and $5.17 million going out.

item.title: Fuel costs put city take home vehicles under review
item.description: With fuel prices up, the council started talking about ending take home vehicles for department heads and on call staff.

item.title: Leftover ALDOT grant money will go to drainage and sidewalks
item.description: The council approved an agreement with ALDOT that lets about $20,000 in remaining grant money pay for drainage and sidewalk work.

item.title: Knapsacks for Kids asks for help this school year
item.description: The weekend food program filled 3,800 bags for Hanceville students last school year and now takes donations through Cash App.

item.title: Holly Market is looking for vendors
item.description: Hanceville Parks and Recreation wants craft, gift and food vendors for the December Holly Market, plus someone to play Santa and carriage ride providers.
